extracted.intended_audience: card issuers, industry trade associations, credit unions, legal practitioners, and other commenters on CFPB rulemaking regarding Regulation Z late fees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards used by the CFPB in its final rulemaking on credit card late fees, including data sources, methodologies for estimating collection costs and late fee income, and how determinations apply to Larger and Smaller Card Issuers. Useful for stakeholders preparing comments or complying with §1026.52 revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of confidential supervisory data with disclosure of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency can rely on confidential information in its rulemaking so long as the agency discloses information to allow interested parties to comment on the methodology and general data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB disclosed how it obtained the data, the methodologies used to analyze the data, the number of accounts reviewed, characteristics about the accounts reviewed, and the results of the various studies. When raw data cannot be released, provide aggregate data and detailed methodological description so commenters can evaluate and provide meaningful comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed description of data sources and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the sources of data used, the types of fields employed, relevant years examined, and the specific ways data are used in the analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB detailed four sources used (Y-14; Y-14+; credit card debt collection data from an information order under section 1022(c)(4) of the CFPA; and the Credit Card Agreement Database), described relevant years and why data were appropriate (e.g., Y-14 issuers constituted ~70% of market), and explained specific uses such as calculating ratios of collection costs to late fee income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use representative datasets when estimating market-level metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Select datasets that are representative of the market segment being analyzed (e.g., Y-14 issuers representing ~70% of outstanding balances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB relied on 10 years of Y-14 data from Larger Card Issuers (covering just under 70% of outstanding balances) and supplemented with Y-14+ and other sources to justify estimates for Larger Card Issuers. Explain why the dataset is representative and sufficient for the intended inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure data fields align with regulatory definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use data fields that are clearly worded to collect information relevant to the rule, and ensure consistency between dataset field definitions and the regulation's terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB noted that the Y-14 'total collection cost' line item aligns closely with the rule's definition of collection costs (e.g., 'costs incurred to collect problem credits that include the total collection cost of delinquent, recovery, and bankrupt accounts'). When relying on a supervisory field, confirm its wording and inclusiveness relative to the rule's cost definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust dataset measures when they include out-of-scope components (post-charge-off costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dataset includes costs not relevant to the regulatory cost measure (e.g., post-charge-off collection costs), estimate and subtract the out-of-scope portion to approximate the regulatory concept (pre-charge-off costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB estimated post-charge-off costs using commissions paid to third-party debt collectors for charged-off accounts (derived from debt collection reports) and subtracted an estimated percentage (e.g., 25% in the Proposal, ~20% based on 2021–2022 data) from Y-14 total collection costs to estimate pre-charge-off costs. Use conservative, transparent estimation methods and explain assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define included costs for cost-analysis under §1026.52(b)(1)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §1026.52(b)(1)(i), costs incurred as a result of late payments include costs associated with the collection of late payments, such as notifying consumers of delinquencies and resolving delinquencies (including establishment of workout and temporary hardship arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify which specific collection activities qualify as costs of collecting late payments. CFPB adopted comment 52(b)(1)(i)-6.i to specify these included activities. Issuers relying on cost-analysis must be able to demonstrate that their identified costs are consistent with §1026.52(b)(1)(i) and related commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude post-charge-off collection costs from cost-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection costs to calculate penalty fees under the cost analysis provisions does not include post-charge-off collection costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB clarified (comment 52(b)(1)(i)-2.i) that post-charge-off costs are not part of the costs used to set late fees under §1026.52(b)(1)(i). Where datasets include post-charge-off costs, use a justified method to remove them (see CFPB's commission-based estimate). This clarification applies to all issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of uncollected fees in fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining appropriate fee amounts under cost-analysis provisions, card issuers may consider fees that they are unable to collect (e.g., fees imposed on accounts charged off, discharged in bankruptcy, or required to be waived by law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment 52(b)(1)(i)-5 provides examples of 'uncollected' fees to consider. Fees that a card issuer chooses not to impose or voluntarily waives (e.g., concessions, workout-based waivers) are not relevant for determining the late fee amount under the cost analysis provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about sample selection and subsampling
rubrics_metrics.description: When using issuer-provided account- or portfolio-level data, describe sampling procedures and any subsampling used (e.g., random 40% subsample of account information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB used complete portfolio data for included issuers but only a random 40% subsample of account information. Explain inclusion criteria (non-zero late fee income, collection costs, late fee amounts, total required payments) and justify subsample representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish aggregate metrics when raw data are confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Release aggregate values and summary metrics that allow stakeholders to compare and analyze without disclosing confidential raw data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB's Revenue-Costs Report included (1) number of portfolios in aggregate for the month; (2) total number of accounts in these portfolios; (3) aggregate interest revenue; (4) CFPB's estimate of pre-charge-off collection costs, total account balances, and weighted ratio of late fee income to estimated pre-charge-off collection costs. Provide similar aggregates so commenters can reproduce or critique analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for reporting variation across institutions but assess materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that reporting practices may vary across reporting institutions (e.g., inclusion/exclusion of overhead, commissions), but evaluate whether such variation materially affects regulatory estimates or thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry commenters argued Y‑14 reporting varies; CFPB determined variations do not undermine reliance on Y‑14 for estimating collection costs for Larger Card Issuers, given the alignment of the Y‑14 field with the rule and the dataset's breadth. Document known variations and perform sensitivity analysis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for timing alignment of costs and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating cost-to-fee ratios, align fee income in a month with estimated pre-charge-off collection costs attributable to that fee income using an appropriate lag structure (e.g., estimating costs that occurred two through six months later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB compared each month's late fee income for a portfolio to the portfolio's average estimated pre-charge-off collection costs for that month, where the estimate was based on costs occurring two through six months later. Explain and justify chosen lag windows and aggregation periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct statistical analyses (e.g., discontinuity tests) on random subsamples to assess behavioral effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use randomized subsamples from account-level data to test for behavioral responses (e.g., whether lower late fee amount in month seven leads to a discontinuous jump in late payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB conducted a Y-14 seventh-month analysis on a random subsample from 2019 account-level data to investigate discontinuities. Describe sampling, statistical tests, significance thresholds, and robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider potential overstatement of late fee income and test sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether reported late fee income might be overstated due to implicit reversals (e.g., re-aging, conversion to payment plans, debt settlements) not captured as explicit fee reversals, and assess impact on cost-to-fee ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB acknowledged possible overinclusion but determined it would not significantly affect the pre-charge-off cost to late fee income ratio. Where plausible, perform sensitivity analyses to show the effect of implicit reversals on key metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple complementary data sources to support rulemaking conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on a combination of supervisory data, supplemental issuer data, information order responses, and contract/agreement surveys to triangulate estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB used Y‑14, Y‑14+, credit card debt collection data (information order), and the Credit Card Agreement Database. Explain how each source informs different parts of the analysis (e.g., income, costs, contract terms) and how they corroborate one another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate supplemental/updated data and explain whether they change findings
rubrics_metrics.description: When additional data become available after a proposal, incorporate them and explain whether they alter original findings or merely supplement support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB received additional months of Y‑14 data and updated commission estimates for 2021–2022; these did not change original findings but were explained to supplement analysis. Document any changes in point estimates (e.g., moving from 75% to 80% pre-charge-off share) and discuss implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor design: not a fee cap—allow issuer-specific cost analyses to exceed safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory safe harbor amount is not a cap; if an issuer's demonstrable pre-charge-off collection costs exceed the safe harbor, the issuer may charge a higher amount consistent with the cost-analysis provisions and applicable requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB stated that the $8 safe harbor is discretionary and issuers may charge higher fees if their own cost-analysis (consistent with §1026.52(b)(1)(i) and §1026.52(b)(2)) demonstrates higher pre-charge-off costs. Provide procedural requirements for documentation and enforcement showing consistency with cost-analysis provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider differential treatment for Smaller Card Issuers where data are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: If data equivalent to supervisory datasets are lacking for smaller issuers, evaluate whether proposed changes should apply to them; refrain from adopting changes for smaller issuers absent sufficient evidence of cost similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB defined 'Smaller Card Issuer' as an issuer with fewer than one million open credit card accounts and did not adopt the $8 safe harbor or elimination of annual adjustments for these issuers at this time, citing lack of equivalent Y‑14 data. Solicit data from smaller issuers and analyze agreement reviews that suggest smaller issuers charge lower late fees.
